title: Sarah
lead: The wife of Abraham, barren into old age, who laughed at the promise of a son and then bore Isaac at ninety. Isaiah calls Israel to look at Sarah who gave them birth (Isaiah 51:2), and the New Testament remembers her as a free woman, a mother of the promise and a model wife (Galatians 4:21–31; 1 Peter 3:6).

sections.b: Isaiah comforts the exiles by pointing to Abraham and Sarah: God made one barren couple into a people, and he can do it again (Isaiah 51:1–3; compare 54:1). Paul quotes God's promise "at this time ... Sarah will have a son" (Romans 9:9) and uses Sarah, the free woman, as a figure of the covenant of promise (Galatians 4:21–31). Hebrews 11:11 may name her faith, though many read it of Abraham's. 1 Peter 3:5–6 holds her up to Christian wives. Later Jewish tradition counts her among the seven prophetesses (Megillah 14a).
